why: For each bar, the widest rectangle of its height reaches from just after the previous smaller bar to just before the next smaller bar. A stack of increasing heights finds both at the moment a bar is popped, so the whole histogram is solved in one pass.
hints: Suppose the rectangle's height is exactly heights[i]. How far left and right can it stretch?
Until the nearest strictly lower bar on each side: previous smaller and next smaller element.

Keep a stack of indices with increasing heights and append a 0-height sentinel. When height[i] < height[top], pop top: its right limit is i, its left limit is the new top + 1; area = height * (i - left). O(n).
pitfalls: Without a final 0 sentinel, bars still on the stack at the end are never measured.
When the stack becomes empty after a pop, the rectangle extends to index 0.
